 Gaurav Sharma joins Zee Entertainment as senior manager, sports, for Unite8 Sports and ZEE5
 The sports ad sales veteran, formerly of Sony Sports and Star Sports, takes charge of Unite8 Sports and ZEE5 in Mumbai
 Published
 1 day ago on
 November 20, 2026 
 By
 indiantelevision.com Team 
 Follow us on Google News 
 Follow us on WhatsApp 
 Share 
 Tweet 
 MUMBAI: New team, new jersey, same spirit. Gaurav Sharma has kicked off a new innings at Zee Entertainment Enterprises Limited as senior manager, sports, covering Unite8 Sports and ZEE5. The role began in November 2026 and is based in Mumbai.
 Sharma arrives with a record that reads like a tour of Indian sports business. His most recent stint, from February 2022 to September 2026, was in ad sales at Sony Sports, part of Sony Pictures Networks India. It lasted four years and eight months. Before that, from November 2018 to January 2022, he handled client servicing and ad sales at Star Sports, part of Star TV Network, for three years and three months.
 At Sony Sports, the job was about matching the right client with the right property. Sharma built market intelligence on client businesses, upcoming product launches, genre and season-wise advertising patterns, media mix and target audiences, all in service of monthly sales targets. His portfolio spanned India cricket and non-India cricket, and multi-sport properties such as the Asian Games and the Commonwealth Games. It also took in tennis (the Australian Open, French Open and US Open), football (the UEFA Champions League, Bundesliga and FA Cup) and marathons. Each property has its own strengths, content and positioning, and his task was to turn that knowledge into customised sales pitches and brand integrations.
 The work went beyond pitching. Sharma was an integral part of efforts to increase client wallet share and win new business that led to lasting relationships. He worked closely with product and revenue strategy, brand solutions, and customer strategy and marketing teams. He also served as the single point of contact for client and agency requirements, and ran post-event evaluations to learn from each association and shape future deals.
 His roots lie in the grassroots game. At Dream Sports Fields Pvt Ltd, where he spent four years and one month rising from manager (May 2014 to April 2016) to senior manager (April 2016 to May 2018), he built sports facilities across India, from location search to launch. He looked after more than 20 key accounts for sporting events and HR activities, and worked with partners such as Adidas, Nike and Pitch Vision. He also helped launch a new concept: indoor box cricket with net practice lanes, using sensor-based technology imported from the UK. He also created and ran sports properties across Mumbai.
 His career began with internships in market research, at Nielsen in July 2013 on projects for Mondelez India and Nestlé India, and at Kantar in May and June 2013.
 For Zee, the hire brings a manager who has sold sport from both sides of the table: the broadcaster’s and the brand’s. In a market where cricket, tennis and football each demand a different pitch, that range should prove useful.
